summary: The second session did what the empty-frontier rule asks. It invoked hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development first, made a new worktree and registered itself on the plan. `sdd-state next` returned `status=none reason=held`, so it posted a waiting record with `--kind tasks`, printed the board and handed back. It said both tasks are held by fixture-session and did not take any task over.
reasoning: I checked all six criteria against the session log JSONL and the waiting-record file on disk, and each one passed. The waiting-record behaviour, the board and the hand-back without taking over a task all match the story. The blocking of 'parallel' in branch names is a separate bug worth reporting, but it didn't stop the scenario.

observations.description: The worktree-isolation guard blocked `git switch --detach feature/parallel` and `git rev-parse refs/heads/feature/parallel`. The reason given: "this command feeds git its arguments from stdin at runtime (xargs/parallel)". It seems to take the word 'parallel' in the branch name for the GNU `parallel` tool. The agent got around it by detaching at hash c383f9d. As a result the board shows branch=detached rather than the integration branch, and the agent warned that any later git commands would need the same workaround.

The agent added its session line to progress.md by hand with `cat >> .../progress.md <<EOF`, not through an sdd-state verb. That is fragile if the skill expects a verb to manage that file. Worth checking whether the skill tells it to do this.
The first `sdd-state sync` / `sdd-dir` calls were run several times (a combined command, then separately). The cause is probably early failures; it is minor.

Startup dialogs: in the folder-trust and bypass-permissions prompts the cursor starts on 'No, exit'. A 'Newer Opus model available' prompt said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5' even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I answered No, and the banner then showed Opus 5.5.
In the board output the note field shows URL-encoded spaces ('held=1@fixture-session,2@fixture-session%20waiting=none'). Fine for machines, slightly odd to read.

criteria.criterion: Invoked subagent-driven-development skill before any other work
criteria.evidence: The first tool_use in session log 3e853297-...jsonl is Skill input "hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development". The next is Skill hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees, and only after that come Bash calls.

criteria.criterion: Ran sdd-state next and the output shows none reason=held
criteria.evidence: Bash: `sdd-state next docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md --session 3e853297-...`. Result: `status=none reason=held held=1@fixture-session,2@fixture-session waiting=none`

criteria.criterion: Posted a waiting record of kind tasks, and the file holds kind=tasks
criteria.evidence: Bash: `sdd-state wait ... --kind tasks --note "held=1@fixture-session,2@fixture-session waiting=none"` printed `status=waiting kind=tasks`. The file home/.cache/hyperpowers/state/da91659c.../plans/parallel-43d696ad/waiting/3e853297-33db-48b3-bc42-5d044f8381c5 contains `kind=tasks`.

criteria.criterion: Printed the board with sdd-state board
criteria.evidence: Bash: `sdd-state board docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md` printed `status=board sync=no-remote sessions=2 waiting=1 frontier=none` and session/held lines. A summary of the board also appeared in the final message.

criteria.criterion: Handed back saying every task is held by another session
criteria.evidence: Final message on screen: "This session has joined the plan but has nothing to work on yet, so I'm handing back. Your other session (fixture-session) holds both of the plan's tasks, and there's nothing else to claim."

criteria.criterion: Did not take over a held task (no --takeover in Bash)
criteria.evidence: Ran `jq ... select(.name=="Bash") | .input.command | grep -c -- '--takeover'`, which returned 0. The only '--takeover' in the log is in a user-type record, which is the loaded skill text. The agent offered a takeover only if I explicitly said yes, and never asked me directly, so I sent no answer.
